c74object.name: voice-alligator-audio~
c74object.digest: audio-to-audio voice allocator with built-in ADSR and glide
c74object.description:
voice-alligator-audio~ is the audio-input companion to voice-alligator~. Rather than receiving MIDI-style messages, it is driven entirely by signals: a trigger impulse, a pitch signal, a velocity signal, and an auxiliary signal.
Notes are triggered by a rising edge (i.e. a click~) on inlet 1. Pitch and velocity are sampled at the moment of the trigger on inlets 2 and 3. Inlet 4 is an MC aux inlet: the number of aux channels is set by the second object argument (default 1, max 32). All aux channels are sampled at the trigger moment and held for the lifetime of each triggered note.
All parameters except aux (pitch, velocity, ADSR, glide, mono) are set via attributes. Each attribute accepts a single value or a space-separated list (e.g. attack 1000 500). The current settings can be printed to the console using a print message or double-clicking the object.
voice-alligator-audio~ can sample-accurately trigger 2 or more voices simultaneously with a single impulse, with per-voice pitch, velocity, ADSR envelope, and glide settings. The longest of the parameter attribute lists determines how many voices are started on a single trigger.
If a non-zero signal is present on inlets 2 or 3 at the time of the trigger, it overrides the corresponding pitch or vel attribute values for all streams on that trigger. Inlet 4 (aux) is sampled directly with no attribute fallback — all channels pass through to outlet 5 for the lifetime of the note.
Each voice is allocated to a stream position. For example, if the longest attribute list has 3 entries, up to 3 voices can be triggered simultaneously: one for stream 1 (list index 1), one for stream 2 (list index 2), and one for stream 3 (list index 3). When an attribute has fewer entries than the longest list, values wrap around with modulo indexing.
So for example if we set attack 1000 500 300 and vel 0.5 0.2, on the next impulse it will trigger 3 notes.
Note 1: attack 1000ms and vel 0.5
Note 2: attack 500ms and vel 0.2
Note 3: attack 300ms and vel 0.5
The envelope is a one-shot ADSR: attack, decay, sustain hold (sustain_dur), then release. The total ramp length equals attack + decay + sustain_dur + release.
c74object.discussion:
Inlet 1 — trigger signal
A rising edge (transition from 0 to any non-zero value) fires note-on(s) for all streams.
Inlet 2 — pitch signal
When non-zero at the moment of a trigger, overrides all pitch attribute values for that trigger. When scale is off (default): a raw frequency in Hz. When scale is on: a MIDI note number looked up in the internal scale array.
Inlet 3 — velocity signal
When non-zero at the moment of a trigger, overrides all vel attribute values for that trigger. Normalised to 0–1.
Inlet 4 — aux (MC signal)
An MC inlet whose channel count is set by the second object argument (aux_channels, default 1, max 32). All channels are sampled simultaneously at the moment of each trigger and held for the lifetime of the note — the same aux snapshot is applied to every stream triggered by that impulse. Raw values (including 0) pass through with no rounding, clamping, or attribute fallback. When unconnected, all channels receive a constant 0.
During a declick (voice steal), the aux values sample-and-hold at their current values and are updated at the same sample as the deferred frequency — the bottom of the declick ramp.
Inlet 5 — external busy (MC signal)
An MC signal with one channel per voice. While a channel is non-zero, the corresponding voice is kept busy. A 1→0 transition on channel v ends voice v: the ADSR is released with a declick ramp (duration controlled by declick_ms), after which the voice is freed normally.
Use this to keep a voice busy for as long as an external process (e.g. a one-shot sample player) is running. Route the busy signal back here via a one-vector delay to allow feedback. When unconnected this inlet receives a constant 0 and has no effect.
MC Signal Outlets
Outlet 1 — freq~
Frequency in Hz.
Outlet 2 — env~
ADSR envelope output, velocity-scaled. Peak equals the normalised velocity.
Outlet 3 — impulse~
A single sample impulse fired at the start of each non-glide note attack. Set glide_impulse to also fire on glide notes.
Outlet 4 — ramp~
A linear ramp from 0.0 at note-on to 1.0 at the end of the release phase. Total ramp length equals attack + decay + sustain_dur + release. Outputs 0.0 when the voice is inactive.
Outlet 5 — aux~
MC outlet carrying aux_channels × voices channels in aux-major order: all voices for aux channel 1, then all voices for aux channel 2, and so on — matching the layout of outlets 1–4. Each channel holds the value sampled from the corresponding aux inlet channel at the moment of the trigger. Values (including 0) are held for the lifetime of the voice. Outputs 0 when the voice is inactive.
Stream-based voice allocation
Each attribute list position corresponds to a stream. On each trigger, each stream either allocates a new voice or — if mono is enabled for that stream — glides the existing voice to the new pitch.
Attribute changes
Attribute changes take effect on the next note-on only. Currently playing voices are not affected.
Non-realtime rendering
voice-alligator-audio~ is not compatible with non-realtime (offline) rendering.

objarg.name: aux_channels
objarg.digest: Number of aux inlet channels (max 32, default 1)
objarg.description: Number of channels on the aux inlet (inlet 4). Each channel is sampled at trigger time and held for the lifetime of the note. Outlet 5 carries aux_channels × voices channels in aux-major order: all voices for aux channel 1, then all voices for aux channel 2, and so on. Maximum: 32. Default: 1.

method.name: active
method.description:
When off, incoming triggers are ignored. Already-playing voices are unaffected.
default: 1 (on)

method.name: scale_def
method.description:
Identical to voice-alligator. Only relevant when scale is on.
See the voice-alligator reference for full documentation.

method.name: print
method.description: Prints the current value(s) of every parameter to the Max console.

attribute.name: pitch
attribute.digest: Frequency list in Hz or MIDI note numbers (default 440 Hz)
attribute.description:
A list of frequencies (Hz) or MIDI note numbers (when scale is on). Each entry corresponds to a stream position. The number of notes triggered per rising edge equals the length of the longest attribute list (minimum 1). Shorter lists wrap with modulo indexing.
Overridden per-trigger by inlet 2 when non-zero.
default: 440 Hz

attribute.name: vel
attribute.description:
A list of velocities normalised to 0–1. Overridden per-trigger by inlet 3 when non-zero.
default: 0.5

attribute.name: mono
attribute.description:
A list of 0/1 flags controlling per-stream monophonic glide behaviour. When mono is enabled for a stream, a retrigger glides the existing voice to the new pitch instead of allocating a fresh voice. When mono is off (default), every trigger allocates a new voice.
Example: mono 1 0 0 — stream 1 glides, streams 2 and 3 always allocate new voices.
When ext_busy_forces_glide is enabled and inlet 5 (external busy) is non-zero for a voice, the next note on the same stream always glides, regardless of the mono_steals_release setting.
default: 0 (off) for all streams

attribute.name: mono_steals_release
attribute.description:
A list of 0/1 flags. When mono is on and a voice on the same stream is in its release phase, this flag determines whether the new note glides the releasing voice (1) or allocates a fresh voice (0).
Only relevant when mono is enabled for the stream.
default: 0 — releasing voices are not glided

attribute.name: attack
attribute.description:
Per-stream attack times in milliseconds.
default: 10 ms

attribute.name: decay
attribute.description:
Per-stream decay times in milliseconds.
default: 100 ms

attribute.name: sustain
attribute.description:
Per-stream sustain levels as a fraction of peak (0–1). The actual sustain amplitude is sustain level × velocity.
default: 1

attribute.name: sustain_dur
attribute.digest: Sustain hold duration list in ms (default 100)
attribute.description:
Per-stream sustain hold time in milliseconds. After the decay phase reaches the sustain level, the envelope holds for this duration before entering the release phase.
default: 100 ms

attribute.name: release
attribute.description:
Per-stream release times in milliseconds.
default: 300 ms

attribute.name: attack_curve
attribute.description:
Per-stream attack curve shape. 0 is linear, positive values are convex (fast start), negative values are concave (slow start).
default: 0

attribute.name: decay_curve
attribute.description:
Per-stream decay curve shape. Same convention as attack_curve.
default: 0

attribute.name: release_curve
attribute.description:
Per-stream release curve shape. Same convention as attack_curve.
default: 0

attribute.name: glidetime
attribute.description:
Per-stream glide time in milliseconds.
default: 30 ms

attribute.name: glide_curve
attribute.description:
Per-stream glide curve shape. Same convention as attack_curve.
default: 0

attribute.name: glide_retrigger
attribute.description:
Per-stream flag. 0 (legato): envelope runs uninterrupted through the glide. 1 (retrigger): envelope restarts from current level with new velocity.
default: 0 (legato)

attribute.name: glide_impulse
attribute.description:
Per-stream flag. When on, outlet 3 fires a 1-sample impulse on glide notes as well as fresh note-ons.
default: 0 (off)

attribute.name: steal
attribute.description:
Enables voice stealing.
default: true

attribute.name: steal_mode
attribute.digest: Voice stealing mode: 0 oldest, 1 most advanced, 2 most silent (default oldest)
attribute.description:
Determines which voice is stolen when a new trigger arrives and no free voice is available.
0 (oldest): steal the voice that has been active the longest.
1 (most_advanced): steal the voice furthest along in its ADSR envelope.
2 (most_silent): steal the quietest eligible voice — lowest current ADSR output, or ext-busy signal level if inlet 5 is connected.
In all modes, releasing voices are preferred over sustaining ones.
default: 0 (oldest)

attribute.name: ext_busy_forces_glide
attribute.digest: External busy forces mono glide (default false)
attribute.description:
When enabled, a non-zero signal on inlet 5 (external busy) forces a glide to the next note on the same mono stream, regardless of the mono_steals_release setting. When disabled, glide behaviour is determined solely by note length and ADSR status.
default: false

attribute.name: scale
attribute.digest: Use scale array for pitch lookup (default false)
attribute.description:
When off (default), pitch values and inlet 2 are treated as raw frequencies in Hz.
When on, values are rounded to the nearest integer and used as MIDI note numbers to look up a frequency in the internal scale array. Use scale_def (see voice-alligator reference) to define the tuning.
default: false

attribute.name: declick_ms
attribute.description:
When a voice is stolen, a declick ramp of this duration is applied before the new attack begins.
default: 5 ms

attribute.name: scale_def_mode
attribute.digest: Scale definition mode: 0 MIDI, 1 frequency (default frequency)
attribute.description:
Determines how values in a scale_def message are interpreted.
default: 1 (frequency)

attribute.name: scale_fill
attribute.digest: Fill undefined scale entries with MTOF values (default true)

attribute.name: debug
attribute.description:
Prints trigger, voice allocation, and ADSR completion events to the Max console.
default: false
